notMigrated.title: ⏳ This page has not been migrated to the cross-platform frontend yet ({0})
notMigrated.body: The cross-platform frontend (Avalonia) currently covers the main window plus the settings window shell and the General page; the remaining tabs exist only in the WPF build. This is a known gap, not a broken feature.
notMigrated.hintWindows: Workaround: on Windows use the WPF build (the one the installer ships) — it is feature complete.
notMigrated.hintOther: Workaround: edit app/backend/config.json directly for the settings this page would expose, or wait for a later release to migrate it.

inference.title: 🎛️ Inference (sampling)
inference.topPTip: Candidate pool; lower is more focused
inference.repeatTip: Higher curbs repetition, too high sounds stiff
inference.profileTip: The Fast / Balanced / Quality profiles set the initial context, the usable share of the ceiling, the batch size and the thread preference; saving a change rebuilds the model.
inference.profileFastTip: Lower context, larger batch and every logical thread, for a faster first token.
inference.profileBalancedTip: The recommended default, balancing first-token latency against long-context capacity.
inference.profileQualityTip: Full usable context and a larger initial window, with an F16 KV cache, at the highest memory cost.
inference.contextNoModel: No model loaded yet: the native and usable context will appear once a model is ready.
inference.contextNativeUsable: Native context {0} tokens · usable {1} tokens · batch {2}
inference.contextTip: The native context comes from the model file header; the usable value is also bounded by the native window, hardware memory and the configured ceiling.
inference.clarifyVagueTip: Ask first when the request is unclear
inference.saveTip: Writes the four sampling parameters, the preset, the context strategy and both switches to config.json
inference.resetTip: Put this parameter back to its default (press Save to apply)
inference.readHint: These values are written to config.json when saved and survive a restart.

agent.title: 🤖 Agent
agent.intro: In agent mode the model decides which tools to call and in what order until the task is done; every step (tool, arguments, result, timing) shows up in the conversation, and Esc stops it at any time.

mcp.title: 🔌 MCP servers (external tools)
mcp.intro: An MCP server is an external process you configure yourself: once connected, the tools it offers appear in the tool list above and the agent can call them.
mcp.security: ⚠️ Security: MCP tools are always treated as sensitive — you must tick them in the tool permissions above before the agent may call them, and no environment variables are passed through by default (secrets such as HF_TOKEN are not handed over). Only connect servers you trust.
mcp.autoConnectTip: When ticked, saving/starting really launches these external processes; when not, they are started on demand.
mcp.timeoutRange: ⚠️ The timeout must be between {0} and {1} seconds
mcp.stagedHint: Changes take effect after “💾 Save” or “🔌 Connect and fetch tools” (tools are re-registered immediately, no restart needed).
mcp.readyHint: Changes apply as soon as you press “💾 Save”: tools are re-registered, no restart needed.
mcp.saveTip: Write this section to config.json and re-register the tools right away (no restart needed)
mcp.connectTip: Save the current configuration, launch the external processes and fetch their tools (same as /mcp connect)
mcp.addExampleTip: Fill in the bundled example examples\mcp\echo_server.py (command python) to verify the path end to end

automation.platformBannerTitle: ⚠️ Automation is not available on this platform ({0})
automation.platformBannerBody: Intranet automation drives the local Microsoft Edge and is currently provided on Windows only. This is a platform limit, not a missing dependency — installing any package will not make it work on Linux/macOS. Workaround: run the automation on a Windows machine and copy the results folder over; everything else (chat, document handling, retrieval, agent) works normally here.
automation.helpPlaceholderBody: Put the cursor into any input below (or click the ? next to a field) and this panel explains that field in plain words, with an example. The full guide is at docs\<locale>\AUTOMATION_GUIDE.md in the release package.
automation.pickDetailTip: Opens the first task automatically, then you click the attachment name on the detail page
automation.pickLoginTip: After signing in, click an element on the page that only appears once you are signed in (for example the user name in the corner)
automation.loginHint: Automation keeps its sign-in state (cookies and so on) in a separate browser data directory that is never shared with your everyday browser. On the first run the program opens the browser so you can sign in manually; after that the state is reused, so you do not sign in again every time.
automation.clearLoginTip: Deletes the browser data directory reserved for automation; the next run asks you to sign in manually again
automation.clearLoginConfirm:
Clear the automation sign-in state?

Afterwards the next run asks you to sign in manually once in the browser window that opens.
(This does not affect your everyday browser and does not delete any result files.)
